newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast plans end-season cocoa quality seminar.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast plans end-season cocoa quality seminar.

text.p: Ivory Coast will hold a seminar on cocoa quality before its 1997/98 marketing season (Oct-Sept) in response to concerns voiced at an industry meeting in Ivory Coast last month, a cabinet statement said on Wednesday.

"A national seminar (is planned) on the quality of produce before the start of the next cocoa campaign," said the statement, which listed points raised by International Cocoa Organisation, industry and donor officials.

Ivory Coast held a second round of Consultative Committee talks in Abidjan on February 5-7 under the terms of a World Bank Agricultural Sector Adjustment Credit but did not issue full details of findings.

Delegates said discussions focused on bean quality problems since liberalisation of internal cocoa marketing in 1995, including a practice of blending poor quality and small midcrop (May-Sept) beans with export quality beans.
A proposal to introduce of different levels of cocoa prices according to reflect quality would be considered along with requests for more reliable marketing data, said the statement.
Rules encouraging overbidding for export contracts on Ivory Coast's donor-sponsored auctioning system, introduced in May 1996, also dominated discussions, delegates said.

"Innovations introduced have had certain negative effects not taken into account which must be given particular attention," said Wednesday's cabinet statement. "The system of allocating export contracts...needs further reforms," it added.
Fulfilment of contracts could be ensured by "the creation of a support fund or guarantee to ensure confidence in the forward sales system," the statement said.
Ivory Coast has refused to release auction trading data requested by the World Bank for considering the merits of rule change options.

Other concerns over fulfilment of contracts by exporters, auction penalty rules, cocoa sack quality and problems arising from chemical fumigation of cocoa for export were also being considered, said the statement.
The World Bank said in February it would review agriculture reforms in April.
Ivory Coast's next Consultative Committee meeting, when auction rule changes will again come under scrutiny, has been pencilled in for May.
